FROZEN_TU.txt - UNT batch 25, TEST seat TU: THE UNDO AT GROWING TIPS AND WHAT CLOSES IT.
Written 2026-11-20T09:37:06Z (date -u) BEFORE ANY CODE EXISTS for this seat and before any batch-25 result or note was read.
Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), maximum effort. ONE MODEL FAMILY. Brief sha256 57bf1444...775c3 (verified). Spec: rank 1, seat TU.
Read before freezing (evidence the brief names; results there are not mine): batch-18 chair, IGS seat/check and IGS notes 1-5,
batch-18 brief, batch-11 chair next_tests, batch-7 brief (THE COMMON PROTOCOL), RN's frozen definitions A1-A12, PD-06/11/18/24/29/30/32,
rule text native_full_h.py l.343-353, 398-480, 595-642 (as text only). No principal definition is chosen below.

A. DEFINITIONS (fixed now)
A1 GRAPH AND BIRTH (rule text l.343-353, 398-417, 420-430). Two-kind four-link graph, one bit per link. Birth by owner r: one link at
   each of r's four neighbours o_1..o_4, r's own link among them; the other three cut links (s_i,o_i) end on three distinct placed
   sites. GUARD: exactly two of the four cut links ON. IMAGE: cut links go; TWIN joins the o's; HEIR joins r and the placed sites;
   each new link copies its cut link's bit; newborns unwritten.
A2 CUT RULE (pending definition, on-file control rule): among guard-passing cuts the TIGHTEST (tight3 = number of the 3 pairs of placed
   sites sharing a neighbour before the Birth), ties uniform. tight3 < 3 = FALLBACK (share reported). No guard-passing cut = failed
   attempt. Second criterion (fewest uncovered loops) NOT applied (deviation D1, as on file).
A3 RIGHTS (PD-06, PD-07A, PD-18, PD-30, PD-17, PD-25, PD-29). k0 = 8 random start sites hold the right. A growth point attempts a Birth
   at rate 1; the right passes owner -> heir; unwritten heirs fire. NEW GROWTH POINTS: each write makes one carrier on the written
   site; it takes up to 10 uniform hops along ON links (modelling step: fixed hop budget, no exclusion, no clock for hops) and is used
   up at the first site it ARRIVES at that has no standing Birth as owner, holds no right and is not its write site (start sites
   included, PD-30); tally 2 makes that site a growth point (PD-25). A carrier with no eligible site in 10 hops (or no ON link) is
   PARKED (counted, lost to the run). No gate test at absorption (modelling step); a growth point with no guard-passing cut sleeps
   until a link at it or at a neighbour changes (sleep device, modelling step).
A4 THE TIP UNDO (rule text l.432-480 implemented literally on the CURRENT graph; PD-24 children first; PD-11/PD-38). A standing Birth
   (owner r, heir H, twin T) may be undone iff H and T are unwritten, hold no carrier tally, neither has a standing Birth as owner,
   H and T are not linked, r is a neighbour of H, and a matching of H's four neighbours to T's four exists with: no such link already
   present, equal bits on the two child links of each pair, exactly two ON, and r's other three neighbours all among T's neighbours
   (owner witnesses the cut). Every open Birth (H, T unwritten and tally-free, no standing child Birth, bits never flipped) is TRIED
   at rate u; among valid matchings one is drawn uniformly (identity or the swap; modelling step). The owner takes the right back.
A5 WRITE: each unwritten newborn is written at rate w (never undone). A written newborn closes its Birth for good.
A6 FLIP LOCK (PD-32, real bit flip; primary and only reading run unless budget allows the flag control): each unwritten newborn with
   two ON links switches ONE of them OFF at rate f (uniform choice); the bit changes at both ends. This closes the Birth's undo exactly
   (bits unequal). When a one-ON newborn is written its home count is 2 and it switches ON one OFF link at once (preferring a
   neighbour below its own home count: home 2 written, 1 unwritten; else a neighbour at home; else none) - modelling step. No other
   flips (modelling step). So f also thins the ON links the guard needs: reported, not hidden (fallback share, stalls).
A7 CLOCK (modelling step): continuous time (Gillespie); rates in units of one Birth attempt per growth point. Everything also against N.
A8 START (supplied input): diamond torus, 8 primitive cells a side, N0 = 1024, all written, two-ON, direction pattern {0,1} ON scrambled
   by 4 x N0 closed alternating-loop flips (own worm). Seeds 2501, 2502. Growth to 64x (65,536 sites).
A9 GRID (registered): u in {0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9} x w in {1, 0.1, 0.01} x f in {0, 0.1, 1, 10} = 48 points, two seeds = 96 runs.
   UNDO-OFF BODY of a point = the u = 0 run with the same w, f (seed means).
A10 RULERS at 64x (and 16x). LABEL: rho = mean eccentricity over 8 seeded centres / (2 (N/2)^(1/3)); ball ratio to the unbounded diamond
   at radii 2..floor((N/2)^(1/3)); 3D-LIKE iff 0.67 <= rho <= 1.5 and all ball ratios in [0.5, 2]; STRAND iff rho > 1.5; else OTHER.
   WALK: exact simple-walk evolution from 4 seeded sources, P(2t) = sum_x p_t(x)^2 averaged over sources, local slopes
   d = -2 dlnP/dln(2t) on octaves 8-16, 16-32, 32-64. WALK READING = mean of the last two slopes. PLATEAU iff the three slopes span
   <= 0.4; CLIMB iff last - first > 0.5. Controls, same code: diamond torus 16,000 sites, square sheet 128x128, random two-kind
   four-link graph 16,384 sites.
A11 STRETCH: 12 start marks; 12 GROWN marks placed at 4x on written non-start sites (any non-start site if fewer exist; pairs with a
   removed mark are dropped and counted). D = mean pair distance. HEADLINE STRETCH = ln(D_64x/D_4x)/ln 16 on grown marks; start-mark
   exponent 1x-64x beside it. EVEN iff the median per-pair exponent >= 0.6 x the headline AND the top tenth of pairs carries < 30% of
   the summed distance gain; share of pairs that got closer reported.
A12 STILL INTERIOR (the common measure): links present at 32x between sites present at 32x; share absent at 64x, binned by the link's
   depth (least distance of an end from a growth point at 32x): 0-1, 2-3, 4-7, 8+; and the share of 32x sites whose four links are
   all unchanged.
A13 SEAM (measuring device only; no rule reads it): start sites labelled by half of the torus (two flat seams); a newborn copies its
   owner's label. MIXED-LINK SHARE = links joining different labels / all links, at every doubling (random mixing gives 0.5).
A14 UNDOABLE SHARE AND FROZEN SET at 64x: every standing Birth classed as UNDOABLE NOW (passes A4) / RETRACTABLE (blocked only by
   standing children none of which is frozen) / JAMMED (A4 fails only on the matching or witness test) / FROZEN (written, flipped,
   tally, or a frozen descendant). LIQUID sites = newborns of UNDOABLE or RETRACTABLE Births. Reported: the four shares; liquid site
   share; largest connected liquid cluster; frozen subgraph: share in its largest component and mean number of frozen neighbours per
   frozen site (4 = solid, about 2 = threads). Executed undos and swaps per net Birth; swap-allowed share among passed undo tests.
A15 KILL CHECK as operated (spec wording kept): a grid point with u > 0 DIFFERS iff, on seed means against its undo-off body, the
   walk reading differs by > 0.25 OR rho differs by > 0.25 OR the headline stretch differs by > 0.03. CLAUSE 1 (the undo changes
   nothing) = no point differs. A differing point is SCRAMBLE-TYPE iff its walk reading is higher AND its headline stretch is lower
   than its undo-off body. CLAUSE 2 = at least one point differs and every differing point is scramble-type. KILLED iff clause 1 or
   clause 2. A point whose difference is smaller than the two-seed spread of either body is flagged WITHIN SEED NOISE beside the
   letter-of-the-spec result. OFF THE TRADE (the 'if it holds' line) = PLATEAU with walk reading > 2.4 AND headline stretch > 0.2 AND
   EVEN, in both seeds.
A16 BUDGET RULE (0281: <= 1800 CPU-s in all, process time summed over every process). Order: validators and controls; seed 2501 full
   grid; seed 2502 in the order u = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9. A run is CAPPED at 75 CPU-s (reached size reported); STALLED after 20,000
   failed attempts in a row or no event possible. If the ledger passes 1,650 CPU-s the remaining runs are DROPPED and listed. If a
   reduction is needed before launch (timing smoke on unregistered seed 7 only), it is written as an ADDENDUM file before any
   registered run.

B. PREDICTIONS (P = my probability; seed means at 64x unless stated)
P1 Undo-off body at w = 1, f = 0: walk reading 1.6-2.4 (P 0.75); no plateau near 3 (P 0.9); headline stretch 0.10-0.24 (P 0.7);
   label not 3D-LIKE (P 0.65); last-doubling old-link cut share 0.2-0.5 overall (P 0.7), deepest bin >= 0.1, so no still interior (P 0.7).
P2 u = 0.1: no point differs from its undo-off body (P 0.6).
P3 u = 0.9, w = 0.01, f = 0 (the most liquid point): walk reading >= 3.0 and CLIMB (P 0.65); rho < 0.6 (P 0.6); headline stretch
   lower than undo-off by > 0.03 (P 0.7); mixed-link share at least twice the undo-off value (P 0.6).
P4 Where a closer is fast (f = 10 at any w; or w = 1 with f >= 1) no u differs from undo-off (P 0.7).
P5 Executed undos per net Birth follow q/(1-q), q = u/(u + 1 + 2w + 2f), within a factor 2 wherever q < 0.3 (P 0.5).
P6 KILL CHECK: clause 1 (P 0.03); clause 2 (P 0.60); survives by the letter (P 0.37); a point OFF THE TRADE in both seeds (P 0.05).
P7 Liquid site share at 64x below 5% at every point with w >= 0.1 or f >= 0.1 (P 0.7); largest liquid cluster <= 20 sites there
   (P 0.6); at w = 0.01, f = 0 the liquid share is 5-60% (P 0.6).
P8 HUNCH (a fourth closer, 'jamming'): at w = 0.01, f = 0, u >= 0.5 at least 20% of standing Births that are unwritten, unflipped
   and childless fail the literal undo test because another Birth cut a link the undo needs (P 0.4).
P9 Flips thin the guard's ON links: at u = 0, w = 0.01 the fallback share at f = 10 exceeds that at f = 0 by >= 0.1 (P 0.55);
   at least one f = 10, w = 0.01 run STALLS before 64x (P 0.35).
P10 The swap is allowed in >= 60% of passed undo tests on grown tips (P 0.7).
P11 The regime boundary (frozen versus liquid) sits where executed swaps per net Birth pass about 0.25: every point above it is
   scramble-type, every point below 0.05 does not differ (P 0.5).

C. WHAT WOULD KILL THE IDEA: A15 clause 1 or clause 2. WHAT WOULD COUNT FOR IT: any OFF-THE-TRADE point in both seeds (then eight
   seeds are owed and are named as the next test if the budget cannot carry them). Negative results are reported as prominently.

premises.claim: A root matches its four neighbours to four distinct same-side sites, itself among them (the local cut).
Birth image: cut links go, each child link copies its cut link's bit, newborns blank; no link joins the two newborns.
Who may give birth; guard: exactly two of the four cut links ON.
The undo: blank newborns, not linked, all 4! reconnections tried on the CURRENT graph; no existing link, equal bits, two ON, owner witnesses, identical forward image.
Single link flips are native moves.
Carriers hop only along ON links; admission and release at a site.
The common protocol (start, cut rule, clock, measures M1-M7).
Tightness = number of the 3 pairs of placed sites sharing a neighbour; census 44/60/0/4; home counts 1 and 2; PD-17 books reading with k0 = 8, hop 10.
The undo is identity or one swap; unstopped it scrambles supplied bodies (IGS-01, IGS-02); the flip lock was left out (checker C2).
Spec TU and its kill line.
LF's independent whole-body walk on its own regrown bodies (1.86 / 1.83 at write 1; 1.70 at write 0.1) and its fall-off rule of thumb.

method.summary: Own event-driven growth code (python3 -I, standard library, no numpy). Two-kind four-link graph with one bit per link; Births by the rule text's local cut with the guard; tightest-first cut rule; rights only at growth points, handed to the heir; new growth points by carrier absorption (two carriers, any unfired site); the rule text's undo implemented literally on the current graph under children-first and tried at rate u on every open Birth, drawing uniformly between the valid reconnections (identity or swap); each unwritten newborn written at rate w; PD-32 as a real bit flip at rate f. Start 1,024-site scrambled two-ON diamond torus; growth to 65,536 sites (64x). Definitions A1-A16 in the frozen text are the method as run.
method.grid_as_run: The full registered grid, NOTHING DROPPED: u in {0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9} x w in {1, 0.1, 0.01} x f in {0, 0.1, 1, 10} = 48 points, seeds 2501 and 2502 (96 runs), all reached 64x, none stalled or capped. By addendum 1, beside it: seeds 2503 and 2504 on the full grid (96 more runs, noise) and an exploratory extension E of six points toward the liquid side (u up to 0.99, w down to 0.001; 12 runs). By addendum 2: slice readings on six points x two seeds (12 re-runs; every re-run reproduced its stored run's counters exactly).

validators.reading: 108 local cuts, 36 pass the guard, tightness 44/60/0/4 at every sampled site (on-file R77 and batch-4 X2 counts reproduced). Every one of 3,132 guard-passing cuts has exactly two valid undos, the identity and the hand-rule swap (two non-owner links carrying the bit opposite to the owner's); the identity undo restores the graph in 3,132 of 3,132. Graph consistency (four distinct links, symmetric bits, ON counts) asserted at the end of every run; two-ON preserved exactly when flips are off.

method.controls_note: Diamond 2.95 (plateau), square sheet 1.97 (plateau), random four-link graph 5.4 then 7.8 then saturating at 2.9 on 16,384 sites - so my frozen CLIMB flag (last minus first slope) can miss a scrambled body; the largest octave slope is reported beside it (addendum 1).
deviations: D1 second cut criterion (fewest uncovered loops) not applied (as on file).
D2 carriers: fixed budget of 10 hops along ON links, no exclusion, no hop clock, no gate test at absorption (modelling steps; frozen A3).
D3 flips: only the PD-32 switch-off of an unwritten newborn's extra ON link and a switch-on at its write; no other flips (frozen A6).
D4 the undo is closed by the literal bit test, not by a flag; a Birth whose bits were disturbed is counted FROZEN (bits) in the classification although a later flip could in principle restore it.

D5 walk ruler from 4 sources with octaves 8-16, 16-32, 32-64 (on-file seats used 6-8 sources and one more octave). Its seed-to-seed standard deviation came out 0.24 - as large as the spec's 0.25 line. This is the seat's main weakness and decides the letter of the kill check.
D6 marks: 12 start marks and 12 grown marks (the protocol asks for marks; on-file seats used 24); no mark was lost to an undo in any run.
D7 M5 (expansion rate times age) and M6 (loop reach) not computed; beta is reported.
D8 slice readings were not in the frozen file; added by addendum 2 on six points only.
D9 timing smoke on unregistered seed 7 printed its rulers; I saw them before the registered runs (disclosed in addendum 1).

what_closes_the_undo.executed_undos: Executed undos per net Birth follow q/(1-q) with q = u/(u + 1 + 2w + 2f) within a factor 0.58-1.62 at all 36 points (0.6-0.7 at write 1, where carrier absorption and jamming close extra Births; 1.3-1.6 at write 0.01 without flips, where retraction re-opens parents).
what_closes_the_undo.swap: The swap is allowed in only 36-45% of passed undo tests without flips (up to 0.63 at fast flips), against 81-100% on supplied bodies (IGS). Executed swaps per net Birth: at most 0.30 on the grid (undo 0.9, write 0.01, no flips), 0.53 in the extension.
what_closes_the_undo.share_still_undoable_at_64x: 1-9% of standing Births pass the literal undo test at 64x (0.1% at fast flips with slow write); a further 0-22% are retractable (blocked only by unfrozen children); 74-99.9% are frozen for good.
what_closes_the_undo.closers_ranked_example_u0.9_w0.01_f0_see: of 24,190 frozen Births: written newborn 11,763; frozen descendant (burial) 7,635; carrier absorbed on a newborn 4,790. Jammed (literal test fails on witness or matching though unwritten, unflipped, childless): 442.
what_closes_the_undo.two_closers_the_spec_did_not_name: (a) carrier absorption on a newborn (PD-29 makes it permanent); (b) JAMMING: a neighbouring Birth cuts one of the owner's three kept links or changes the twin's neighbours so the owner can no longer witness the cut. Among childless, unwritten, unflipped Births 20-29% are jammed at write >= 0.1 without flips, 3-20% at write 0.01, under 5% at fast flips. A Birth that only cuts one of the heir's three placed links does not jam (the rule text tests the current graph).
what_closes_the_undo.flip: The PD-32 flip closes the undo exactly as stated, and at f = 10 almost nothing is undoable (0.1-1.4%). But it also takes an ON link from an old neighbour: ON links per site fall from 2.00 to 1.54 (write 1) and 0.68 (write 0.01) at f = 10, fallback Births rise from 9% to 59%, and up to 1,600 growth points sleep with no guard-passing cut. what_the_failure_teaches: The undo was the one native move that adds links without adding sites, and the hope was that it could supply the spare routes a body needs to walk above 2. In growth it cannot: every tip is locked within about one Birth time by five separate native closers, and the few swaps that do happen rewire links three steps apart at the tip and are diluted by the next doubling. So spare routes at every scale must come from what a Birth builds or from Births acting together, not from reworking finished Births. A second lesson: the supply (how many growth points per site, set here by the write rate) moves the body far more than the undo, the flip or the cut - stretch 0.02 to 0.16 and seam exponent 0.1 to 0.8 across write rates - yet always along the same curve.
